summary: A 1936 46 ft steel tower with a 7x7 ft metal cab, inside the River of No Return Wilderness; sources disagree on tower size and when use ended, and current access is not established.

facts.design: 7x7 ft metal cab on a 46 ft steel tower (Aermotor MC-40 per Forest Lookouts); a 1959 Coast and Geodetic Survey description gives about 70 ft (disputed)

access.note: NHLR says it is maintained for emergency use. Idaho Fire Lookouts labels it 'Drive-Up Emergency Use' while NHLR places it in the wilderness; no source says it is open to visitors or for rent.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR, firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts and the Forest Lookouts 1936 entry give a 46 ft steel tower (about 14 m). The Forest Lookouts page also quotes a 1959 Coast and Geodetic Survey description of about 70 ft with an 8 ft square, 10 ft high cabin. The record keeps 46 ft; the survey figure is noted but not resolved.

Idaho Fire Lookouts lists relief staffing 1974-1982; firelookout.com says the tower has not been used since the 1970s. The sources do not say when active use ended, so the staffing status is recorded as unstaffed with no date.

Idaho Fire Lookouts labels the site Drive-Up Emergency Use, while NHLR places it inside the River of No Return Wilderness. Not resolved; the record keeps the drive-up label as the source's claim and does not confirm access.

notes_for_editor: Build year (1936) and the 46 ft tower with 7x7 cab agree across four sources. Height (46 ft vs about 70 ft in a 1959 survey description), the end of active use (relief staffing 1974-1982 vs not used since the 1970s), and access (Drive-Up Emergency Use vs a wilderness location) conflict and are not resolved. Current rental or visiting status is not established. Not cited or verified: an AllTrails route page (fetch returned 403) and a trailsoffroad.com search snippet describing a 1914 tower; neither was read. Keeping Watch has a coordinates-only item for this site and was not used as a source for facts. Sources cited in the story are 1-4. The brief record needs no corrections.
